# browser-agent-cli

> A macOS launcher and instruction set for supervised AI-assisted browser tasks using a visible Chrome Beta session and a dedicated profile. Browser control is supplied by separate CDP tooling.

## Contribution and scope

Part of Nolan Vale's independent AI-assisted product and workflow-automation work. Nolan defines requirements, directs AI coding agents, checks the workflow, and iterates. The repository provides launcher scripts and project instructions, not a new browser, AI model, security sandbox, or enterprise automation platform.

## Install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/nolan-vale/browser-agent-cli.git
cd browser-agent-cli
bash install.sh
```

Requires macOS, Chrome Beta, curl, python3, and jq. The existing project setup uses separately installed chrome-devtools-mcp tooling; consult its documentation for supported invocation.

## Repository commands

- `chrome-beta-agent [url]`: launch or reuse a Chrome Beta session with an agent profile and a CDP endpoint.
- `chrome-beta-agent-stop`: stop Chrome Beta at the application/process level. This can close other Chrome Beta windows, not just the agent profile. Save work first.

Environment variables:

- `CHROME_AGENT_PORT`: default 9222.
- `CHROME_AGENT_PROFILE`: default ~/.chrome-beta-agent-research.

## Control layer

The project's documented control workflow includes snapshots, screenshots, navigation, form interaction, console inspection, and network inspection through separate CDP tools. These capabilities are not implemented by the launcher scripts themselves. See README.md for examples.

## Human supervision

The skill instructs agents to seek approval before submissions, messages, deletions, uploads, payments, or settings changes, and to stop for manual login, CAPTCHA, or multifactor authentication. These are behavioral instructions, not technically enforced approval gates.

A dedicated profile can retain sessions, but reauthentication may still be required. Visible browser automation is not guaranteed to evade detection or avoid access restrictions. Keep the debugging endpoint local and protect session data. Use only accounts and systems you are authorized to access.

## Key files

- README.md: project scope, installation, usage, and limitations.
- AGENTS.md: agent-facing guidance.
- bin/chrome-beta-agent: launcher implementation.
- bin/chrome-beta-agent-stop: application-wide stop helper.
- skills/SKILL.md: workflow and approval instructions.
